system.name: Tatoo system
system.note: Tatoo I and Tatoo II drawn as one body at the centre, the two suns side by side in Tatooine's sky, their line square to the sun's path, Tatoo II below (it rises after Tatoo I and sets before it), never overlapping. Tatooine round them in 304 days with its three moons, each on its own orbit; the ringed gas giants Ohann and Adriana farther out, small points by eye. The night-sky sheet of three moons is hidden while this applies (the moons stand for it).

bodies.note: The real pair goes round itself in about 64 hours (the film study); drawn as one body it never does. The separation is the gap between their bright discs' edges.

grounds.note: All desert: a world's dry belt sits near 20 to 30 degrees. A summer time of year: the twins stand high at noon (75 degrees).

system.name: Naboo system
system.note: Naboo round its star in 312 days, with Rori, Ohma-D'un, the small third moon and a fourth of ours (SWG's second moon over Rori). Naboo and Rori stand in the same system: from Rori, Naboo is exactly where Naboo's sky puts Rori. Rori turns (lore is silent; a moon so close would in truth be locked, which would hold Naboo still in Rori's sky: the owner's call).

bodies.name: Naboo (the star)
bodies.note: Its name is only in a fan reference; lore gives it none.

grounds.note: Mild, green lake country round Theed: a temperate belt.
Wetter and swampier than Naboo, frequent rain: a warm, wet low latitude. Rori turns, so the longitude only sets where Naboo rises.

system.name: Corellian system
system.note: Corell and the Five Brothers: Corellia with its three moons (Gus Treta the outermost), Drall, Tralus and Talus (the double world, Centerpoint Station half way between them) and Selonia, in that order out. Talus goes round Tralus locked, so Tralus stands still in Talus's sky (20 degrees up), phases through the day and hides the sun once a day. SWG's red fourth disc over Corellia stands for Drall (lore gives Corellia three moons). Talus's two moons are ours.

system.name: Endor system
system.note: The forest moon goes round the gas giant Endor locked: the giant stands still 30 degrees up in its sky, turns its bands at its own 30-hour day, phases through the game day (full at midnight) and hides the sun once a day. Kef Bir and another of the giant's nine moons go round it farther out. The star is Ibleam (Legends); canon's second star is in the model, not drawn.

system.name: Yavin system
system.note: Yavin 4 goes round Yavin Prime locked: the giant stands still 40 degrees up in its sky, turns its bands, wobbles a little, phases through the game day (full at midnight) and hides the sun once a day. Yavin 8, Yavin 13 and a lesser moon go round the giant farther out; Fiddanl and the comet Stroiketcy round the star, small by eye.

Wasskah and Alaris Prime are in the model, too small to draw. The night-sky sheet of two moons is hidden while this applies.

system.name: Mustafar system
system.note: Mustafar round Priate in 412 days between the gas giants Jestefad (just inside, about 65 degrees from the sun, half lit) and Lefrani (just outside, about 130 degrees from it, gibbous), both on the same side, so they stand in the evening sky together. Both share Mustafar's year, so they stay close beside it as the lore keeps them (at other years the clockwork would carry them to the far side of the star). Nur goes round Mustafar (the owner's ask; canon also puts it round Jestefad).

bodies.name: Jestefad
bodies.note: Inside Mustafar, almost its bigger twin; its field drives storms round Mustafar.

bodies.name: Nur
bodies.note: No land, rough seas, the Inquisitors' fortress.

bodies.name: Lefrani
bodies.note: Outside Mustafar, a fainter, cooler banded globe.

grounds.note: Volcanic everywhere, so the latitude is free; a fairly high sun suits the ash-light. Its 36-hour lore day makes the longest game day, 6 hours.

system.name: Hoth system
system.note: Hoth, sixth out, round its faint blue-white star in 549 days, leaning at least 20 degrees; a late winter time of year gives it a low sun (21 degrees at noon). SWG has no Hoth sky: the star is drawn by us, and the owner's night-sky sheet of three moons goes round as one group. The three moons themselves (unnamed) and the asteroid belt are in the model, not drawn: tick Drawn on each (and untick the sheet's group) to draw them one by one.
